patch.objective: Explain how the baroreceptor reflex keeps blood pressure up on standing, and how the skeletal muscle pump and venous valves return blood to the heart
secondaryObjectives: Identify the brain regions involved in movement (primary motor and somatosensory cortex, basal nuclei, cerebellum, brainstem) and what each contributes

sources.cite: OpenStax, Anatomy and Physiology 2e, 20.4 Homeostatic Regulation of the Vascular System
sources.note: Read 2026-11-17 through a summarizing fetch: baroreceptors sit 'primarily in sinuses (small cavities) within the aorta and carotid arteries'; 'When blood pressure drops too low, the rate of baroreceptor firing decreases', which raises sympathetic stimulation of the heart and vessels; venous return 'is further enhanced by both the skeletal muscle and respiratory pumps'. The page does not discuss standing; that the reflex must catch the fall in pressure when blood pools in the legs on standing is the course objective's own application. In the case, a man with Parkinson disease (which can blunt this autonomic response) becomes light-headed on standing during gait training: seat him at once, measure, and report.

sources.cite: Osborne JA, Botkin R, Colon-Semenza C, et al. Physical therapist management of Parkinson disease: a clinical practice guideline from the American Physical Therapy Association. Phys Ther. 2022;102(4):pzab302. doi:10.1093/ptj/pzab302 (PMC9046970)
sources.note: Read 2026-11-16 in the published article (Phys Ther 2022;102:pzab302) as posted on a University of Oviedo course site (ocw.uniovi.es), through a summarizing fetch that returned quotes; the PMC copy answered a browser check and the publisher's page was not opened. Table 1: physical therapists 'should implement moderate- to high-intensity aerobic exercise', balance training, gait training and 'external cueing to reduce motor disease severity and freezing of gait' (strong recommendations, high-quality evidence); 'should implement behavior-change approaches to improve physical activity' is a moderate-strength recommendation. No dose numbers are taken from it here.

sources.cite: APTA Acute Care and APTA Cardiovascular and Pulmonary, Adult Vital Sign Interpretation in Acute Care Guide 2021 (boards approved March and April 2021)
sources.note: Relayed from the REQ-232 DPT stroke case (read 2026-11-11 through a text extraction of the PDF), not re-read: HR rises about 10 beats/min per MET and recovers in 3-5 min; SBP rises about 10 mmHg per MET; orthostatic hypotension is an SBP drop over 20 or a DBP drop over 10 mmHg within 3 min of standing; stop criteria include an SBP drop over 10 mmHg with rising workload and SpO2 below 90%.
